transcript.text: Can you describe your role and main responsibilities as a Medical Officer at the 120-bed private hospital in Ahmedabad?

I'm an MBBS doctor and have worked for five years, the last three as a medical officer in a 120-bed private hospital in Ahmedabad. I cover outpatient and emergency shifts and make the monthly duty rota for eight junior doctors, though that is an informal duty. I was also part of a hospital committee that reduced the discharge delay from 4 hours to 2.5. That is when I realised how much patient experience depends on operations. I want an MBA to move into hospital management.
How did managing outpatient and emergency shifts with about 40 consultations a shift influence your approach to patient care and time management?
transcript.anchor_quote: I cover outpatient and emergency shifts

transcript.text: Healthcare is a noble field, and I believe in patient-centric care. I would like to leverage my clinical background and transform healthcare delivery with a holistic approach.

I don't agree that doctors are poor at management. We run emergencies, coordinate teams and decide under pressure. What we lack is financial training, and that is what I am asking the MBA for.

transcript.text: I was appointed as the hospital's operations head last year, and I manage the nursing staff and administration. That is my formal role.

feedback.summary: The candidate demonstrates a clear motivation to transition from clinical duties to hospital management, with insightful recognition of the complementary nature of clinical and financial skills. They show practical involvement in operational tasks like duty scheduling and committee work, though specific examples and outcomes were limited by privacy concerns. Some responses lacked depth on personal contributions and impact, and clarifications on leadership scope and challenges could strengthen the profile.
